title: Spontaneous polarization in chemical vapor-deposited polymer films creates large electric fields.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran the paper-context tool: Europe PMC reports the paper is not open access, has no PubMed Central copy, no supplementary file list, no data flag, no database cross-references and no accession numbers anywhere in the indexed text. I searched Zenodo and Dryad for the DOI and the article number 'aeg9547' and both returned 0 records. A web search confirmed the subject matter (polymer thin-film surface potentials from initiated chemical vapor deposition) and found no companion data deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the measurements themselves comes from the abstract alone: that surface potentials arise during film growth, scale linearly with film thickness, are stable in air, are tunable via deposition parameters, and have a polarity set by the choice of polymerization initiator. I never saw a single number, table, or file.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset exists to download. Paywalled Science article with no PubMed Central full text, no supplementary file listing retrievable through Europe PMC, and zero hits for the DOI in Zenodo and Dryad. The measurements live in the paper's figures only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not reached in a meaningful sense: there is no file, so the label (surface potential in volts, or polarization) is not a column anywhere. It would have to be digitized off published plots of potential versus film thickness.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs would be deposition conditions (monomer identity, initiator identity, substrate temperature, filament temperature, pressure, flow rates, thickness). None of these are available as machine-readable fields; they are described in a methods section I could not retrieve.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are unambiguous in principle for this physics (volts for surface potential, nanometres for thickness, degrees Celsius, millitorr), but this is a judgement about the field, not something I verified in any file.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unverified, but a single-laboratory thin-film deposition study of this type typically reports tens of films, not the ~1,500 labelled rows the checklist requires. No row count was visible anywhere.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: well under 1 MB if it existed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Any table of deposition conditions and measured surface potentials would be tiny. Size is the one thing that is clearly not a problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download and no application programming interface record of a dataset to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label would be a direct physical measurement (Kelvin probe or similar surface-potential measurement), not another model's output, so there is no circularity concern. This rests on the abstract's description, not on inspected files.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join is possible: the paper carries no standard biological or chemical identifiers, only polymer and initiator trade names.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: there is no accessible dataset, and the subject (electric fields in vapour-deposited polymer coatings) is materials physics rather than biology, which is outside this project's stated scope.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use polymer film deposition settings to predict the electric surface voltage the finished coating spontaneously develops.
plain_idea.train_on: For each coated sample: which monomer and which chemical initiator were used, the substrate and heating-filament temperatures, chamber pressure, gas flow rates and final film thickness. Number of samples: unknown, and likely only tens.
plain_idea.predict: The spontaneous surface potential of the film in volts, and its sign (positive or negative), measured directly by a surface-potential probe held above the film.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups making coatings for sensors, electronics or implant surfaces would get a recipe-to-voltage lookup instead of trial-and-error depositions. But with no released data and only tens of samples, a simple linear fit of voltage against thickness would almost certainly do as well as any model.

ml_idea: The only project this paper supports would be predicting the spontaneous surface voltage of a vapour-deposited polymer film from its deposition recipe and thickness. It fails immediately: no data was deposited, the sample count is almost certainly in the tens, and the abstract already states the headline relationship is linear in thickness, so a straight line is the model. The paper is also materials physics, not biology, and so sits outside this project's topic filter.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because no data file exists to size. Any such table would be kilobytes and run instantly on a laptop; size was never the obstacle.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Search Zenodo, Dryad and Europe PMC for a deposited dataset tied to the DOI. I did this in one minute and all three returned nothing, which killed the project.

verdict_reason: No data was deposited anywhere (zero hits for the DOI in Zenodo and Dryad, no PubMed Central copy, no supplementary file listing), so Part A1 fails outright. Even if the numbers were released, a single-laboratory thin-film study reports tens of samples rather than the thousands needed, and the abstract already names the governing relationship as linear in film thickness, leaving nothing for a model to learn. The paper is also polymer materials physics rather than biology, outside this project's topic scope.
